problem: Enable repeatable physical policy improvement by giving coding agents reliable reset, rollout and outcome-verification interfaces instead of treating code generation itself as robot research progress.
contribution: ENPIRE is a two-stage harness: humans help construct and validate immutable environment/reset/reward APIs, then agents modify policy/training code from real rollout feedback. Parallel identical stations share hypotheses through Git. Primary PDF is the September 2026 v2 of ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World.
algorithm: EN establishes task interfaces and feedback using demonstrations/human critique; PIRE then alternates policy refinement, physical rollouts, logged reward analysis and hypothesis selection. Agents may combine procedural skills, BC and offline/online RL. Distributed agents run asynchronously and merge useful recipes; environment APIs remain immutable during policy search.
observations: Top-down and two wrist RGB-D streams, robot proprioception and task-dependent force/torque estimates; GPU insertion adds a side RGB-D camera. Pin verification fuses visual alignment, insertion height and estimated force, and zip-tie verification uses two views to reduce single-view false positives.
actions: Policies issue joint targets at 30 Hz through the provided controller; lower-level YAM tracking is 100 Hz. Agents edit training/policy code and invoke reset/rollout APIs. The paper's existing bounded-force grippers and fixed control setup are hardware features, not settings transferable to SO101.
embodiment_and_data: Eight identical bimanual YAM stations, each two 6-DoF CAN arms with a 1-DoF gripper and an RTX5090 32GB/128GB RAM workstation. Real Push-T, pin insertion, GPU insertion and zip-tie cutting; simulation PushT and RoboCasa365. Disk-finalized episodes retain action-source labels and route human/manual data separately from online RL data.
experiments: Compares agent backbones/harnesses, heuristic and gradient-based policy improvement, and fleet sizes 1/4/8. Human-guided environment construction precedes autonomous PIRE. Main success metric permits eight feedback-conditioned retries within one rollout, unlike independent one-shot precision. Pin target is 50 consecutive successful episodes. Simplified Push-T vision ablations use relaxed success regions and 10-degree orientation tolerance.
baselines: Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh, Claude Code Opus4.7 High and Kimi K2.6; pin comparison to PLD-RL human-in-loop recipe; RoboCasa GR00T N1.5 and zero-shot CaP-X; native vision versus callable-image-understanding versus no visual access on simplified Push-T. Compute/fleet and training recipe can differ, so identify the comparison when citing gains.
quantitative_result: PDF p7 section3.3 reports one-to-eight stations reduces Push-T time to normalized score1 from roughly5h to2h, and pin time to near-perfect success from >1.5h to about40min. These are stated approximate curve results, not a paired confidence interval. Figure2 p2 and appendix B.6 p20 attribute +10.8 percentage points to BC regularization in an example idea tree. Page5/A.2 p16 reward implementation latency budget is under150ms. Exact final task-by-task success denominators are NOT_EXTRACTED; do not interpret abstract99% as single-attempt success across all tasks.
limitations: Substantial one-time human work is needed for validated reset/reward/environment construction; the immutable interfaces and force-capable YAM system are prerequisites. Resource utilization is incomplete; larger fleets reduce per-robot utilization and increase token cost superlinearly. Eight retries conflate precision with recovery. Reward-design held-out snapshots may be inspected for failures during development, so separate a fresh final audit. Provided PDF code snippets2/3 appear to repeat a generic prompt rather than executable implementations.
code_and_license: Primary PDF p1 links https://github.com/NVlabs/ENPIRE and research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/enpire. Repository, model and data licenses were not independently inspected. Copyright on PDF is NVIDIA2026, all rights reserved; it does not establish a code/data license. No code inspected or executed.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT the immutable episode interface, finalized directories, action-source provenance, hypothesis ledger and independently assessed visual outcome verifier. NX16GB/SO101/ROSMASTER are materially different from each32GB5090 station and CAN torque-capable YAM. Keep existing controller settings; camera-only demonstrations remain unvalidated for outcome, grasp force and autonomous reset until supported by actual evidence.

algorithm_detail: Each station's FastAPI supports separately identifiable rollout buffers; Git carries code/results across a decentralized fleet. Human feedback first establishes reset/reward; the agent then owns a streamlined writable learning codebase and chooses BC, RL or procedural hybrids. SERL-style deployment/actor/learner processes use finalized disk episodes; RL transitions enter online replay and human/manual labels enter demonstration replay. Explicit markdown summaries transfer research experience to a new task after raw trajectories/checkpoints/transient logs are removed. Canonical simulation removes state-leaking/oracle/repeated-reset APIs.
integration_contract: Represent environment version, task/reset/verifier versions, episode ID, action source per step, synchronized camera timestamps, policy commit and immutable evaluation configuration. Grant a policy experiment only supported rollout interfaces; finalized episode boundary gates replay ingestion. Report one-attempt success, retry-conditioned rollout success, reset failures and verifier false positives separately; store old failed hypotheses and compute/token/wall-clock cost.
license_evidence: Paper copyright text inspected, repository license NOT_AUDITED; no permission inferred for code, model weights or camera data. API principles may be independently implemented with citations.
required_experiments: Offline label verifier on fresh held-out success/failure videos including occlusion; compare latency and false positives across available views. Measure reset success and human intervention separately. Reproduce a low-cost single-station baseline with fixed episodes and policy versions before parallel optimization; compare recipes under equal interaction/time budgets, preserve all failures, and evaluate on fresh task configurations after selection.
difference_from_explorer: Explorer currently offers one ROSMASTER plus SO101 arms with real legacy control and camera recording, not a validated eight-station autonomous-reset RL laboratory. Adopting a logging/hypothesis interface does not establish ENPIRE performance, force sensing or automatic manipulation reliability.
